devicesPage.title: Connected Devices
devicesPage.subtitle: Connect watches, rings, glucose sensors, and home health devices so BioMath Core can read trends and explain them in plain language.
devicesPage.catalogIntro: All connectable devices are listed here — nothing is hidden behind a filter. Each card shows the signals a device usually provides, so you can pick gear that matches your goals and connect a supported brand below.
devicesPage.signalsIntro: These are the capabilities BioMath Core uses most often when a device is connected.
devicesPage.emptyBrands: Explore the full device guide above, then connect from Cabinet when you are signed in.
devicesPage.chooseBrand: Choose a manufacturer to authorize. Supported families include Apple, Samsung, Google, Fitbit, Garmin, Oura, Ultrahuman, WHOOP, Dexcom, FreeStyle Libre, Withings, Omron, and more.

recommendations.title: How to choose
recommendations.intro: If you do not own a device yet, start with the outcome you care about most:

values.sleep: Oura Ring, Ultrahuman Ring, WHOOP, or Eight Sleep
values.activity: Apple Watch, Garmin, Samsung Galaxy Watch, Fitbit, or Polar
values.glucose: Dexcom G7 or FreeStyle Libre (continuous glucose)
values.blood_pressure: Omron or Withings BPM (validated cuff-style monitors)
values.long_term: Smart rings and recovery bands worn day and night
values.universal: Apple Watch or Samsung Galaxy Watch plus a smart scale

continuous_glucose.title: Continuous glucose
continuous_glucose.body: Day-long glucose curves from CGMs — useful for meals, energy dips, and metabolic patterns.

sleep_stages.title: Sleep stages
sleep_stages.body: Duration, deep/REM balance, and overnight consistency from watches, rings, and sleep systems.

hrv_recovery.title: HRV & recovery
hrv_recovery.body: Heart-rate variability and recovery scores that hint when to push and when to rest.

blood_pressure.title: Blood pressure
blood_pressure.body: Home cuff readings that track vascular comfort over weeks — not a one-off snapshot.

body_composition.title: Weight & composition
body_composition.body: Smart scales for weight, lean mass, and body-composition trends.

activity_load.title: Activity load
activity_load.body: Steps, workouts, and strain so load can be balanced with recovery.

smartwatch.title: Smartwatches
smartwatch.body: All-day heart rate, sleep, activity, and often ECG or SpO₂ on the wrist.

smart_ring.title: Smart rings
smart_ring.body: Discreet 24/7 wear for sleep, HRV, temperature, and recovery.

recovery.title: Recovery bands
recovery.body: Strain and recovery focused bands worn continuously.

cgm.title: Continuous glucose
cgm.body: Clinical-style sensors that stream glucose without finger sticks for most of the day.

blood_pressure.title: Blood pressure monitors
blood_pressure.body: Validated home cuffs for reliable systolic/diastolic tracking.

body_composition.title: Smart scales
body_composition.body: Weight and body-composition estimates for longer trends.

sleep_home.title: Home sleep systems
sleep_home.body: Bed-based tracking for sleep quality and overnight vitals without a wrist device.

apple_watch.name: Apple Watch
apple_watch.blurb: Broad everyday coverage: heart rate, HRV, sleep, SpO₂, ECG, and workouts.
apple_watch.connect: Wear your Apple Watch and open the Health app on your iPhone. In BioMath Core, choose Apple Watch and approve sharing for heart rate, sleep, activity, and related metrics.
apple_watch.syncs: Heart rate, HRV, sleep stages, SpO₂, ECG (where available), workouts, and activity load.
apple_watch.tip: Keep the watch on overnight so sleep staging and morning readiness have a full picture.

samsung_galaxy_watch.name: Samsung Galaxy Watch
samsung_galaxy_watch.blurb: Wrist metrics plus select models with cuffless blood-pressure support where available.
samsung_galaxy_watch.connect: Pair the Galaxy Watch with Samsung Health on your phone. In BioMath Core, authorize Samsung Health for the metrics you want to share.
samsung_galaxy_watch.syncs: Heart rate, HRV, sleep, SpO₂, activity, ECG, and blood pressure on supported models.
samsung_galaxy_watch.tip: Complete any Samsung Health calibration steps for cuffless blood pressure before expecting those readings.

garmin.name: Garmin
garmin.blurb: Training load, recovery, sleep, and HRV suited to endurance and structured sport.
garmin.connect: Sync your Garmin with Garmin Connect. In BioMath Core, link Garmin Connect and approve training, recovery, and sleep metrics.
garmin.syncs: Heart rate, HRV, sleep, activity, training load, recovery, and stress scores.
garmin.tip: Open Garmin Connect once after workouts so BioMath Core receives the latest training files.

google_pixel_watch.name: Google Pixel Watch
google_pixel_watch.blurb: Fitbit-backed sleep and activity with a compact smartwatch experience.
google_pixel_watch.connect: Keep Fitbit / Google Fit syncing on your phone. In BioMath Core, authorize Fitbit-backed metrics from your Pixel Watch.
google_pixel_watch.syncs: Heart rate, sleep, activity, SpO₂, and everyday movement patterns.
google_pixel_watch.tip: Charge before bed or keep overnight wear consistent so sleep trends stay comparable week to week.

oura.name: Oura Ring
oura.blurb: Ring-based sleep staging, readiness, temperature, and HRV.
oura.connect: Wear the Oura Ring and open the Oura app. In BioMath Core, authorize Oura for sleep, readiness, and recovery metrics.
oura.syncs: Sleep stages, HRV, resting heart rate, temperature trends, readiness, and activity.
oura.tip: A snug overnight fit improves temperature and HRV quality for recovery insight.

ultrahuman.name: Ultrahuman Ring
ultrahuman.blurb: Lightweight ring for sleep, recovery, and metabolic-leaning daily signals.
ultrahuman.connect: Pair the Ultrahuman Ring in its companion app. In BioMath Core, authorize Ultrahuman for sleep and recovery signals.
ultrahuman.syncs: Sleep, HRV, heart rate, temperature, and recovery-oriented daily scores.
ultrahuman.tip: Wear continuously for a few days so recovery baselines settle before comparing days.

whoop.name: WHOOP
whoop.blurb: Continuous strain, recovery, and sleep coaching without a traditional screen.
whoop.connect: Wear WHOOP and keep the WHOOP app synced. In BioMath Core, authorize WHOOP for strain, recovery, and sleep.
whoop.syncs: Strain, recovery, sleep performance, HRV, resting heart rate, and activity load.
whoop.tip: Leave the band on during workouts and overnight so strain and recovery stay aligned.

dexcom_g7.name: Dexcom G7
dexcom_g7.blurb: Continuous glucose with frequent updates for meal and energy pattern insight.
dexcom_g7.connect: Follow Dexcom setup for sensor warm-up. In BioMath Core, authorize Dexcom to share continuous glucose readings you approve.
dexcom_g7.syncs: Continuous glucose curves and related time-in-range style trends for educational insight.
dexcom_g7.tip: Note meal times in your own routine so glucose swings are easier to interpret later.

freestyle_libre.name: FreeStyle Libre
freestyle_libre.blurb: Flash/continuous glucose sensing for day-to-day metabolic awareness.
freestyle_libre.connect: Activate the FreeStyle Libre sensor in LibreLink / Libre app. In BioMath Core, authorize Libre glucose sharing.
freestyle_libre.syncs: Flash or continuous glucose readings for day-to-day metabolic awareness.
freestyle_libre.tip: Scan or keep the phone nearby as your Libre model requires so gaps stay short.

omron.name: Omron
omron.blurb: Widely used validated blood-pressure cuffs for home monitoring.
omron.connect: Pair your Omron cuff with the Omron Connect app. In BioMath Core, authorize Omron for blood-pressure readings.
omron.syncs: Systolic, diastolic, and pulse readings from home cuff measurements.
omron.tip: Measure at a consistent time, seated and rested, for cleaner week-to-week trends.

withings_bpm.name: Withings BPM
withings_bpm.blurb: Connected cuff readings that sync cleanly into a health history.
withings_bpm.connect: Connect Withings BPM in the Health Mate / Withings app. In BioMath Core, authorize Withings blood-pressure data.
withings_bpm.syncs: Validated cuff blood-pressure readings and related pulse metrics.
withings_bpm.tip: Use the same arm and posture each session so comparisons stay meaningful.

withings_body.name: Withings Body+
withings_body.blurb: Smart scale for weight and body-composition trends.
withings_body.connect: Step on the Withings scale while it is linked in Health Mate. In BioMath Core, authorize weight and body-composition metrics.
withings_body.syncs: Weight, BMI, and body-composition estimates such as fat and muscle trends.
withings_body.tip: Weigh at a similar time of day, ideally mornings, for smoother trend lines.

eight_sleep.name: Eight Sleep
eight_sleep.blurb: Bed system tracking sleep stages and overnight vitals.
eight_sleep.connect: Keep the Eight Sleep Pod online in the Eight Sleep app. In BioMath Core, authorize sleep and overnight vitals.
eight_sleep.syncs: Sleep stages, overnight heart rate, HRV, and bed temperature signals.
eight_sleep.tip: Leave the cover powered and connected overnight so stages and vitals sync by morning.

fitbit.name: Fitbit
fitbit.blurb: Accessible sleep, heart rate, activity, and stress tracking.
fitbit.connect: Sync your Fitbit with the Fitbit app. In BioMath Core, authorize Fitbit for sleep, heart rate, and activity.
fitbit.syncs: Heart rate, HRV, sleep, activity, stress, and SpO₂ where the model supports them.
fitbit.tip: Enable overnight sleep tracking in Fitbit settings so BioMath Core receives full nights.

polar.name: Polar
polar.blurb: Sport-grade heart rate, training load, and recovery metrics.
polar.connect: Pair Polar with Polar Flow. In BioMath Core, authorize Polar for heart rate, training, and recovery.
polar.syncs: Heart rate, HRV, sleep, activity, training load, and recovery metrics.
polar.tip: Sync Polar Flow after sessions so recovery and load update before morning guidance.

explain.howBody: We only request access to health metrics. We do not see or store logins and passwords. You can disconnect the device at any time.
explain.point1: The app collects authorized metrics from your device
explain.point2: We interpret trends and suggest calm next steps
explain.point3: Data can inform reports and Health Guide guidance
explain.privacyBody: You stay in control. We never receive your device password and cannot control the device. We only receive the health data you authorize.

authorize.title: Grant access
authorize.intro: Allow the device to transmit metrics automatically.
authorize.syncBody: Default: daily in the morning. You can change this later:

success.title: Device connected
success.body: BioMath Core will update metrics and use them in recommendations and reports.
success.tipBody: Regular wear helps us track direction — improving, declining, or stable — not only a single day.

footer.howBody: Authorized metrics (sleep, heart rate, stress, recovery, glucose, and more) are collected and explained in plain language. We focus on trends and practical next steps — not raw dumps of numbers.
footer.privacyBody: You control the connection. We do not know your device password and cannot control the device. Disconnect anytime.

seo.title: Connected Devices — Wearables & Sensors | BioMath Core
seo.description: Connect watches, rings, glucose sensors, blood-pressure cuffs, and smart scales. BioMath Core reads the trends and explains them in plain language for your reports and Health Guide.

live.label: Living signals
live.title: Your body sends quiet data all day
live.body: BioMath Core listens across {{categories}} categories and {{devices}} connectable devices — then turns trends into calm, practical guidance for reports and Health Guide.

flow.label: How connection works
flow.title: Authorize, sync, understand
flow.body: You grant access to metrics only. Trends flow into personal context for reports and Health Guide — educational guidance, not a diagnosis.

authorize.title: Authorize metrics
authorize.body: Choose the manufacturer and approve which health metrics may be shared. We never receive your device login or password, and you can withdraw access at any time.

sync.title: Sync on your schedule
sync.body: Daily, a few times a day, or near real-time where the device supports it. Syncing runs quietly in the background and you can change the rhythm whenever you like.

guide.title: Guide & reports
guide.body: Trends appear in your reports and give Health Guide context for calm, practical suggestions. Everything stays educational — it is never a diagnosis.

connection.body: gives BioMath Core more precise signals. We do not only collect numbers — we explain their meaning and relate them to your state and habits.

deviceHints.opening: You can connect a watch, ring, band, glucose sensor, cuff, or scale. After connecting, BioMath Core updates data and can use it in reports and Health Guide guidance.

success.body: The next sync happens automatically. You do not need to do anything manually.

firstSync.title: Metrics received
firstSync.body: We will track the trend, not just single values.

why.title: Why this matters
why.body: Devices help notice changes early. Think of them as a calm navigator for load, recovery, and gentle adjustments — before symptoms become the first alert.

token_expired.title: Access expired
token_expired.message: Device access has expired. Refresh access so metrics can be read again.

no_data.title: No new data
no_data.message: The device did not send new data today. It may not have been worn or synced. We will try again automatically.

service_error.title: Manufacturer unavailable
service_error.message: The manufacturer is temporarily unavailable. We will retry syncing later.

manual_disconnect.title: Device disconnected
manual_disconnect.message: The device is no longer sending data. You can reconnect anytime.

bluetooth_sync.title: Phone sync
bluetooth_sync.message: The device may not have synced with the phone yet. Open the manufacturer app — the rest usually follows automatically.

sleep_declined.title: Sleep quality decreased
sleep_declined.message: Recent sleep has been less deep. This may reflect nervous-system load. We can suggest gentle recovery steps.

sleep_improved.title: Sleep improved
sleep_improved.message: Sleep looks more stable — a good sign that recovery is improving.

hrv_improved.title: HRV improving
hrv_improved.message: Heart-rate variability improved — a sign the nervous system is recovering.

hrv_declined.title: HRV decreasing
hrv_declined.message: The nervous system may be running hot. Gentle recovery mode is often the better next step.

activity_high.title: Elevated load
activity_high.message: Load is higher than usual — keep recovery in view.

glucose_unstable.title: Glucose fluctuations
glucose_unstable.message: Glucose is swinging. We can help relate meals and habits to the pattern — without diagnosis language.

blood_pressure_stable.title: Blood pressure stable
blood_pressure_stable.message: Stable, normal readings support vascular comfort over time. If readings rise, we explain calmly without fear language.

healthGuide.title: How Health Guide uses device data
healthGuide.template: Based on your latest device data, we see a trend ____________. This is not a diagnosis, but an important signal. Would you like an explanation and recommendations?
healthGuide.agreeBody: I will explain in two ways: (1) physiological analysis (Opinion A) and (2) behavioral and lifestyle explanation (Opinion B). You can compare them and choose what fits.
healthGuide.secondOpinionBody: A second opinion helps view the same signals from physiological and adaptive angles — like two specialists with different thinking styles.

whyDevicesMatter.title: Why connected devices matter
whyDevicesMatter.description: A single measurement is a snapshot; a device shows direction. When sleep, recovery, glucose, and load are followed over weeks, small shifts become visible long before they turn into complaints — and gentle adjustments are usually enough.

realTimeBehavior.title: How data behaves once a device is connected
realTimeBehavior.description: Metrics arrive on the schedule you choose and are compared with your own recent baseline, not with an average stranger. What you see is the direction of change: improving, steady, or drifting.

continuousMonitoring.title: Continuous view:
continuousMonitoring.description: Between syncs nothing is lost — readings are collected in the background and summarized when you open BioMath Core, so you never have to log anything by hand.

dataInfluenceReports.title: How device data shapes your reports
dataInfluenceReports.description: Authorized metrics become part of the personal context behind every report. Instead of raw tables you get the trend, what likely influenced it, and a short list of practical next steps you can actually follow.

dataInfluenceAI.title: How device data reaches Health Guide
dataInfluenceAI.description: Health Guide reads the same trends you see, so answers reflect your recent sleep, recovery, activity, and glucose patterns instead of generic advice. It explains; it does not diagnose.

secondOpinion.title: Second Opinion:
secondOpinion.description: The same signals can be read two ways — a physiological explanation and a behavioral, lifestyle one. Seeing both helps you decide what fits your week instead of accepting a single verdict.

alertsNudges.title: Alerts and gentle nudges
alertsNudges.description: Notifications stay rare and calm. You hear from us when a trend holds for several days, not when a single night looks unusual — and every message explains what it means and what to do next.

positiveReinforcement.title: Progress counts too:
positiveReinforcement.description: Improvements are highlighted just as clearly as declines, because knowing what worked is the fastest way to keep it going.

userSettings.title: You choose how often data is read
userSettings.description: Sync frequency is yours to set, device by device. Pick the rhythm that matches how you wear it — you can change it at any time without losing history.

onlyAtNight.title: Only at night
onlyAtNight.description: Best for rings and sleep systems. Data is read once after your night, so the day stays quiet.

onlyInTheMorning.title: Once each morning
onlyInTheMorning.description: A single daily summary of sleep, recovery, and yesterday’s load. The calmest option for most people.

everyFewHours.title: Every few hours
everyFewHours.description: Useful during training blocks or busy weeks, when load and recovery shift within a single day.

continuously.title: Near real-time
continuously.description: For continuous glucose sensors and recovery bands, where the shape of a curve matters more than a daily number.

userSettings.footer: Whatever you choose, syncing stops the moment you disconnect a device, and past data stays in your history until you delete it.

advancedBehaviorNote.title: A note on how far this goes
advancedBehaviorNote.description: BioMath Core reads what your devices report and explains it in context. It does not control your device, does not replace clinical measurement, and never issues a diagnosis — use it as background for better conversations with your clinician.

realScenarios.title: What this looks like in practice
realScenarios.description: Below are everyday situations built from real device data — what the numbers showed, how Health Guide explains them, and the tone we use. Read them to see how guidance stays calm, specific, and free of alarm.

general.title: How every scenario is handled
general.safeBody: Nothing here names a condition or predicts illness. Signals are described as patterns, and any reading outside a normal range is a reason to speak with a clinician, not a conclusion in itself.
general.trendsBody: One restless night or one high reading changes nothing. A pattern is only mentioned once it holds across several days, which keeps guidance steady instead of reactive.

cgm.title: Continuous glucose sensors
cgm.body: A CGM shows how meals, movement, stress, and sleep shape your day. The value is in the shape of the curve — how high it climbs and how quickly it settles — not in any single number.
bullets: Compares each day’s curve with your own recent baseline
Links rises and dips to meals, movement, and sleep
Waits for a repeated pattern before suggesting anything
Points you to a clinician if readings stay outside your usual range

sleep_hrv.title: Sleep and HRV
sleep_hrv.body: Sleep depth and heart-rate variability describe how well your nervous system recovers. Together they explain why an ordinary week can feel heavy and why an easy week can feel effortless.
bullets: Follows deep and REM balance across the week, not one night
Reads HRV against your own baseline, never a population average
Suggests lighter days when recovery drops for several nights
Confirms what is working when recovery climbs back

activity.title: Activity and load
activity.body: Steps, workouts, and strain only make sense next to recovery. The same training week can be a good stimulus or too much, depending on how your nights look.
bullets: Balances training load against sleep and HRV
Notices a build-up of load before it turns into fatigue
Recognises a well-matched week and says so
Keeps suggestions small: one adjustment at a time

glucoseSpike.title: A sharp rise after meals
glucoseSpike.description: Glucose climbed quickly after lunch on several days this week and took longer than usual to settle back down.
glucoseSpike.response: Your afternoon curve has been rising faster than your own baseline. This is a pattern worth understanding, not a warning. Meal composition and what follows the meal both matter — a short walk after eating often flattens this curve. Let us watch the next few days together.
glucoseSpike.secondOpinion: Read behaviorally, the same curve often follows a rushed meal, a short night, or a stressful morning rather than the food alone. If your sleep has been light this week, the metabolic response is expected — restoring the nights may change the curve more than changing the plate.

glucoseStable.title: A steadier curve
glucoseStable.description: Glucose stayed within a narrow band for most of the week, with gentle rises after meals and a smooth return.
glucoseStable.response: Your curve has been calm and predictable — the rises are moderate and the returns are quick. Whatever your rhythm has been lately, it suits you. Keeping meals and movement in their current pattern is the simplest way to hold this.

recoveryDown.title: Recovery is trending down
recoveryDown.description: HRV has been below your usual range for four nights and deep sleep has shortened, though total time in bed has not changed.
recoveryDown.response: Your nervous system looks like it is carrying more than usual. Time in bed is fine, but the quality of recovery has dipped. This is a good week for lighter training, an earlier wind-down, and less late caffeine. If it persists beyond a week or two, it is worth mentioning to a clinician.
recoveryDown.secondOpinion: From a behavioral angle, this pattern often tracks life rather than physiology — a demanding stretch at work, later evenings, or travel. If any of that matches your week, treat the numbers as a signal to protect your evenings for a few days rather than a sign that something is wrong.

recoveryUp.title: Recovery is climbing back
recoveryUp.description: HRV has returned to your usual range and deep sleep has lengthened across the last several nights.
recoveryUp.response: Recovery is heading back to where it usually sits, and the change has held for several nights, so it is a real shift rather than noise. Whatever you changed recently is working — keeping the same bedtime for another week is the easiest way to make it stick.

overload.title: Load is outpacing recovery
overload.description: Training volume rose sharply this week while sleep stayed the same and recovery scores drifted lower each day.
overload.response: You have added load faster than your recovery has kept up. Nothing here is alarming — it is simply the point where more effort stops paying off. One easier session or one extra rest day this week usually resets the balance.

balanced.title: Load and recovery are matched
balanced.description: Activity stayed consistent through the week and recovery scores held steady alongside it.
balanced.response: Your load and your recovery are moving together, which is exactly what a sustainable week looks like. There is nothing to adjust — this is a good baseline to remember when you plan the next block.

fatigue.title: Quiet, unusual tiredness
fatigue.description: Activity dropped noticeably for several days, resting heart rate is slightly higher than usual, and sleep has been longer without feeling restful.
fatigue.response: Your body is asking for a slower stretch — lower activity with a higher resting heart rate usually means recovery is still in progress. Give it a few gentle days and watch whether things settle. If the tiredness continues for more than a couple of weeks, it is worth discussing with a clinician.
